races.name: Racing TV Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Leopards Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 3yo from Edward Bethell's yard, returning after 13 days with two starts at 7f-8f on Standard ground in form; handles the trip and the Good surface poses no concern, making it the most natural traveller close to Star Of The Desert.

runners_data.name: Star Of The Desert
runners_data.note: Holds a clear mapping advantage as the only front-runner, but Joey Ramsden's stable is 0-from-9 in the last 14 days and the [STYLE_FIT] note flags this position as slightly out of character — the gift of no pace pressure partially offsets that concern.

runners_data.name: Blairtum Night
runners_data.note: Returns from a 225-day break for Linda Perratt, a yard that is 0-from-8 in 14 days, and arrives with a documented tendency to fade in the finish — the combination of absence, weight (139lbs) and stamina doubt makes this a significant each-way risk.

runners_data.name: Rake Lane
runners_data.note: A 4yo with a single run on the board (seventh at 7f on Standard), carrying top weight alongside Blairtum Night; style is entirely unknown, and Mark Walford's modest recent strike rate offers limited trainer confidence despite two wins in 20 from the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bella Angelina
runners_data.note: Third on debut over 7f on Good ground for Harry Charlton, who has one win from ten in the last 14 days; the step up to a mile is an open question but her only run came on identical going and she shaped with enough promise that a forward move is plausible.

runners_data.name: Wid
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up 3yo has the most relevant form profile — a placed effort at 8f on Good ground — and the stable's 7-from-52 recent strike rate is the strongest in the field; depends entirely on the pace being genuine enough to make his late run count over a flat mile.

races.paceDynamic: Star Of The Desert is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger for the lead, should settle into a fully uncontested, controlled gallop from the outset over this flat Carlisle mile on Good ground. Leopards Rock will look to sit prominently just behind, while Wid and Blairtum Night are the confirmed hold-up types who will need the pace to be genuine enough to draw the race out late. With only one horse willing to go forward and no pressure applied, Star Of The Desert can dictate a modest, controlled tempo — the danger is not a fast pace but an artificially slow one that collapses the field into a sprint finish. This shape strongly favours prominent or mid-division runners who can travel close to the action without burning energy fighting for position, and particularly those with enough finishing pace to exploit a tempo that may be too generous to the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of The Desert bowls along uncontested at a fair but unhurried gallop and none of the field has the finishing pace to reel it in.
scenarios.body: Star Of The Desert controls every yard, selects its own fractions, and the modest pace never gives the hold-up horses enough momentum to close the deficit; Leopards Rock, sitting close in second, is the most natural threat given its prominent style and proximity throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fill Podium
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of The Desert and Leopards Rock trade the early sections and both stay close enough to the pace that the late closers simply cannot summon the ground.
scenarios.body: Leopards Rock, comfortable racing prominently on Standard ground and stepping back to a mile it has already handled, tracks the leader with purpose and runs it down close home; the hold-up horses are left with too short a run to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of The Desert sets a searching enough gallop to string out the field and the hold-up horses find the late fractions genuinely fast enough to deliver them.
scenarios.body: Wid, whose best form has come on Good ground at a mile and placed last time at 8f, is the hold-up type most equipped to finish strongly if conditions open up; Blairtum Night carries a big weight penalty and a 225-day absence that makes relying on its finish extremely risky.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets Field
scenarios.trigger: If the unknown quantities among the lightly raced runners — Rake Lane or Bella Angelina — produce a step forward in form that their handlers have been quietly targeting.
scenarios.body: Bella Angelina showed promising form on similar Good going when third at 7f and steps up in trip for a yard that hits with lightly raced types; Rake Lane's style is uncertain but trainer Mark Walford's 2-from-20 in 14 days suggests some quiet confidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Star Of The Desert bowls into an uncontested lead at a genuinely comfortable tempo — if it does, the field will bunch dangerously late and hold-up horses Wid and Blairtum Night are left with insufficient race to close.

Blairtum Night has not run for 225 days and is documented as a horse that fades in the finish — if it travels well early, the risk of a dramatic stoppage is real and could cause interference in a six-runner field.

Bella Angelina and Rake Lane are both lightly raced with unknown tactical flexibility; if either gets outpaced early and drops back through the small field, they could compromise the run of Wid coming from off the pace.

Leopards Rock is the only runner whose style (Prominent) naturally slots it straight onto Star Of The Desert's tail — monitor whether Oisin Orr chooses to sit on the leader's back or allows a gap to open, as that decision will define the complexion of the finish.

Jason Hart on Wid will need to judge whether the pace is genuine enough to launch from the rear — in a race this small with a soft gallop, he may be forced to move sooner than ideal or risk a dawdle that neutralises his horse's finishing kick entirely.

races.name: Molson Coors EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Muckle Handicap

runners_data.name: Wolf Of Badenoch
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer whose recent form includes a third at 8f on good but who has only one placed effort from five runs in similar going; the 23-day break is not a concern for Tony Culhane's yard but his tendency to race from the rear is a handicap when the pace is likely to be modest.

runners_data.name: Fleur De Mer
runners_data.note: Has shown consistent form in staying trips, placed three times in last four over 12-15f including on soft, and Paul Mulrennan is an excellent pilot for a hold-up horse needing a strong gallop; the concern is that good ground is a step up in surface speed from her recent soft outings, though her stable's horse carries headgear (p) which may sharpen her early focus.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: The sole natural front-runner in the field, she arrives on the back of back-to-back wins over 12-13f and the trainer has a 14-day record of 1/2, suggesting live fitness; her 3-day turnaround is short but she clearly thrives when fresh, and her STYLE_FIT flag merely reflects the rarity of her role in this field — here it is an asset, not a weakness.

runners_data.name: Ottoman
runners_data.note: His true preference is to race from the rear, though with so many genuine hold-up types in this field he is likely to end up in midfield by default; a solid second over 12f on good ground 14 days ago is strong recent evidence, the headgear (b) keeps him honest, and Thomas Greatrex rides with confidence, but the trainer's T14 of 0/6 is a sobering stat.

runners_data.name: Hijo De La Luna
runners_data.note: Consistent pattern of finishing in the top half from hold-up positions over middle distances on good ground, though his last six runs show no win and only one placed effort at a similar level; the visor (v) is retained from recent outings and Simon West's 0/1 T14 record offers little encouragement, with the horse pushed forward on the map only because the field has too many closers to show them all at the rear.

runners_data.name: Broadstone
runners_data.note: Absent for 37 days and all five of his last runs came on standard (AW) ground, so this turf good surface is an untested question; John Norton's yard has a modest 14-day record, and the horse's form figures of 9-5400 show a deteriorating profile — he is mapped to midfield as a redistribution artefact, his natural home being the back of the field.

runners_data.name: Due To Shine
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old carrying the lightest weight in the field at 118lbs, which is an advantage Brian Ellison's team will not ignore; 54 days off is the longest gap in the field and his good-ground record is limited (sim-going 0W0P from 3 runs), though a placed effort over 10f on standard and a second over 8f on soft hints at residual ability — his hold-up style is genuine but he is in the midfield map only because space at the rear is fully occupied.

races.paceDynamic: Is She Now is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival willing or able to press her, she is set to dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop over the 1m3f trip on good ground at Carlisle. With the rest of the field comprising genuine hold-up types — Ottoman, Hijo De La Luna, Broadstone, Due To Shine, Wolf Of Badenoch, and Fleur De Mer — the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring closers into the race on merit alone. Several redistributed runners (Ottoman, Hijo De La Luna, Broadstone, Due To Shine) are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield purely because the field is too hold-up-heavy for them all to race at the rear; of these, Ottoman and Due To Shine have shown the best recent form at the relevant trip and are most likely to secure a forward position if any jockey attempts to take closer order. This race shape — a lone front-runner on a fair pace with no pressure — strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles, or hold-up horses with the exceptional finishing speed to overcome a potentially modest tempo, making Is She Now the obvious tactical beneficiary and those riding patiently vulnerable if she is allowed to slip away unchallenged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Is She Now Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Is She Now is allowed to bowl along in front without pressure and controls the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a comfortable gallop, conserves energy through the middle stages, and kicks clear entering the straight before the hold-up horses can close the gap on good ground; her recent wins over 12-13f on good going and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 1/2 underline her fitness for this exact scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the closing runners build a head of steam and overhaul Is She Now in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling tempo paradoxically brings the hold-up horses — who are tracking closer than usual due to redistribution — into the race, allowing those with the best finishing kick to surge past a tiring front-runner late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types secures a prominent midfield berth and times a run to perfection from off the steady pace.
scenarios.body: Ottoman, with a strong recent second over 12f on good going and a jockey who may choose to ride more positively, is best placed to capitalise; his form at this trip and surface gives him a genuine each-way profile if he travels smoothly in the slipstream.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Is She Now sets a frantic early pace or something unexpected forces a contested lead, causing the race to fall apart in the straight.
scenarios.body: A rare contested lead would string the field out and expose Is She Now to tiring, opening the door for whichever hold-up horse has the best acceleration to rattle home late; Due To Shine, placed twice recently at the trip on soft/standard, could emerge as a surprise beneficiary on this ground.

watchPoints.text: Is She Now has run just 3 days ago — watch for signs of flatness or early reluctance to stride on, as any hesitation in front could unravel the dominant scenario entirely.
Ottoman's trainer Greenall & Guerriero have returned 0/6 over the last 14 days — form may be temporarily off, and punters should watch his paddock and early market move carefully.

Fleur De Mer steps up to good ground after recent soft outings; watch the betting market for any drift that might signal the stable's concern about the surface change before committing to a hold-up scenario relying on her.

Several hold-up horses will be competing for the same midfield territory — watch the early positions closely, as any jockey who elects to push forward aggressively (most likely Greatrex on Ottoman or Hardie on Due To Shine) could accidentally inject pace and change the race shape entirely.

Broadstone's 37-day absence combined with an all-AW recent history means his behaviour in the paddock and at the start on turf good ground is worth monitoring for any sign of freshness or unfamiliarity.

races.name: Rachael Bell Wealth Management Handicap

runners_data.name: Catalyse
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Jim Goldie who has struggled for form recently (six and nought from last two), though good going suits and 20 days since last run is fresh enough; Jake Dickson's 7lb claim helps with a light enough weight.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter here, ridden by Andrew Mullen for Iain Jardine whose yard is in solid nick (7/31 last 14 days); has only two wins in similar going across 15 runs which tempers confidence, and racing prominently is within role here but the overall handicap record is modest.

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse for Charlie Johnston who finishes close in good-ground 6f races (five times in the top seven last five); Jason Hart takes a strong book and the horse's profile fits a controlled-tempo race well.

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old is a genuine closer by nature, though placed to midfield here because the rear will be crowded; Duran Fentiman is competent but the horse's best going figures tend to come on a softer surface, and the 30-day break is a minor flag.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's four-year-old has a consistent record in 6f good-ground handicaps (multiple placings), runs from hold-up, and Jonathan England takes the ride; the horse's win came on good and it has hit the frame repeatedly without finding a way past, suggesting it needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner by inclination, carrying a hood, who landed a 5f win on good just 13 days ago; Barry McHugh partners a filly with an excellent similar-going record (3W7P from 15 runs) and she is versatile over trip but meeting a slight question stepping up to 6f.

runners_data.name: Instant Bond
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan rides a horse in good heart — two wins from last six including back-to-back 6f victories on good — and wears a tongue-tie; prominent style suits a controlled pace and good ground, though a 16th two runs ago does require explanation.

runners_data.name: Orbital Chime
runners_data.note: Helen Cuthbert's six-year-old wears a visor and is a true hold-up horse whose best efforts come over 7f; nudged to midfield by redistribution given the crowded rear, and similar-going figures (2 from 15) are modest — Lewis Edmunds rides.

runners_data.name: Henriette Ronner
runners_data.note: A three-year-old wearing a visor, trained by Tony Coyle and Kaine Wood, whose form on good ground is sparse (2 from 11 similar-going) and whose preferred trip looks to be 6f-7f on artificial surfaces; a genuine closer in style, absorbed into midfield here by the weight of hold-up types, which limits its chances of getting the clean run it needs.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's seven-year-old wears a tongue-tie and a pads combination, is a hold-up performer at heart shuffled into midfield, and has strong place form over 5f on good; stepping up to 6f is a mild concern given most of its near-misses come at the minimum trip, and Kaiya Fraser claims.

runners_data.name: Soda
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has placed three times from four runs on good ground but has been stepping down in trip (from 8f to 6f); a natural closer placed into midfield here, it is lightly raced and William Pyle rides — the drop to 6f could sharpen it up, but handicap experience is limited.

races.paceDynamic: Mount Ruapehu is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine leader to push it, is set to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo on good ground over six furlongs at Carlisle. Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond are the likeliest to press from a prominent position, sitting just off the pace rather than challenging for the lead, which means Mount Ruapehu should dictate terms without being seriously harassed through the first half of the race. That controlled pace scenario overwhelmingly favours hold-up horses who can close into a weakening leader from the two-furlong pole, with prominent racers also in a strong position if they conserve energy early. The field holds more true hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Bay Breeze, Henriette Ronner, Orbital Chime, Kyber Crystal and Soda are all genuine closers, but with so many vying for the same ground they have been redistributed to midfield, and the horses most likely to secure genuine prominent berths behind Mount Ruapehu are Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Ruapehu sets a measured, uncontested pace and the field chases without disruption, hold-up horses get a genuine target.
scenarios.body: Mount Ruapehu dictates from flag fall, settles into a rhythm unchallenged, and the closers who find clear runs from two furlongs out can reel in a fading leader; good ground at Carlisle does not exaggerate pace, so the timing suits those arriving late with momentum.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow or Instant Bond track Mount Ruapehu tightly and kick before the hold-up horses get into gear.
scenarios.body: The prominent pair conserve energy behind a moderate tempo then hit the front early in the straight, giving closers too much to do; Instant Bond's recent 6f form on good and Miss Rainbow's sharp recent win make both credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Mount Ruapehu is allowed to coast to the two-furlong mark virtually unchallenged before injecting a kick.
scenarios.body: In a true dawdle-and-sprint scenario Mount Ruapehu's positional advantage proves decisive, with the hold-up horses unable to close the gap in time on a track that does not heavily favour closers when the tempo is very modest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position disrupts the field and the hold-up horses find clear runs simultaneously through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Multiple closers arrive in a wall of horses late, and the winner emerges from the pack rather than from the front; this scenario is discounted because most of the true hold-up types are unlikely to secure ideal position or unobstructed runs given how congested the rear will be.

watchPoints.text: Mount Ruapehu controls all tempo — if Andrew Mullen sets a crawl, the entire race shape changes and prominent horses such as Instant Bond and Miss Rainbow become the primary threats to hold-up types arriving too late.

With Bay Breeze, Orbital Chime, Henriette Ronner, Kyber Crystal and Soda all jostling for the same ground at the rear, traffic problems in the straight are highly likely — watch for a winner emerging wide or racing alone on the outside.

Instant Bond's unexplained 16th-place run two starts ago (on the same going) is a question mark; if that form was a blip, its current shape is strong, but if there is an underlying issue it will not reproduce recent wins.

Miss Rainbow drops back from a 5f win to 6f and wears a hood — if the hood sharpens her early, she could take up a position closer to Mount Ruapehu than her nominal style suggests and turn this into a match between the two.

Carlisle's six-furlong track places a premium on horses who switch off early and finish strongly from two furlongs out — jockeys on Mr Cool, Catalyse and Great should be judged on whether they can find a clear lane before the field fans wide approaching the final furlong.

races.name: British EBF Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies filly who owns a 6f Good win in her recent history and wears a visor, suggesting she can find a concentrated late effort; her hold-up style is genuine and she gets her natural position here, but she needs at least a fair gallop to close the gap on a front-runner with a clear lead.

runners_data.name: Ormolulu
runners_data.note: David Nolan partner who has placed at 6f Goodish ground before, but her true racing style is as a hold-up horse and in this field the rearmost berths are crowded — she is likely to find herself a position or two closer than she'd prefer, which may blunt the finishing effort she relies upon.

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: The race-shaping pivot: Richard & Fahey's three-year-old has two wins at 6f Good in her recent history and maps as the sole front-runner, meaning Ethan Tindall can control tempo without a challenger; her STYLE_FIT note acknowledges the role is slightly stretched, but the track and conditions suit her well enough that the concern is minor.

runners_data.name: D Flawless
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's five-year-old has a genuine 6f win and wears a hood, and Jason Hart is a capable handler of these sprint types — however, her natural preference is to race from behind and with several hold-up horses compressing into the same part of the field, she is likely forced closer to the pace than her best form suggests suits her.

runners_data.name: Rogue Attraction
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old has a win and a second at 6f Good in recent starts, and Oisin Orr gives her a quality jockey booking; she carries a prominent/hold-up hybrid profile (hg:p) and with only 15 days since her last run she arrives fresh enough to be competitive if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Bleep Test
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's busy three-year-old (LR:12d, T14:15/104 confirms yard in strong form) maps prominently and has a placed record at 6f Good four times in five recent starts — she is the logical partner to Cotai Belle in the front group and benefits from the solo pace-setter scenario as she can draft close and pick her moment.

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old ran only three days ago (LR:3d), which is an immediate flag for residual fatigue; her recent 6f Good form reads poorly (sim-going 2/15), she is a true hold-up horse compressed into midfield by the field configuration, and the combined weight of quick back-up and compromised position makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has the most credentialled trainer in the field (T14:10/56) and races with a hood — she has a 6f win at Good in hist and her unbeaten trainer angle warrants respect; her style is unclassified (U) meaning she carries tactical flexibility, and she may prove the most dangerous mid-race threat to the prominent horses.

races.paceDynamic: Cotai Belle is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to force the issue, she should be able to control tempo from the front without being pressured — a sustainable, owner-set gallop on Good ground at Carlisle's straight six. Bleep Test is the only other horse mapping prominently, giving Cotai Belle clean air and the ability to dictate stride pattern, which on this flat six-furlong track with its slight downhill kick is a significant structural advantage. This race shape strongly favours horses who either track the early leader from a handy position or carry enough class to finish powerfully from mid-division off a honest but uncontested pace — pure hold-up specialists will find six furlongs at a measured tempo too short a runway. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear: Ormolulu, D Flawless, and Dandy Magic are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning Cotai Belle's lead is unlikely to be troubled early, and those three may find themselves racing closer than ideal, diluting their finishes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cotai Belle Front Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Belle secures the lead unchallenged and sets a controlled pace that suits her stamina reserve.
scenarios.body: Cotai Belle rolls along comfortably in front on Good ground over her optimum 6f trip with Ethan Tindall getting a clean break — her recent Carlisle and flat-track form (two wins at 6f Good in hist) is directly relevant here, and a horse dictating its own tempo over a trip it handles is notoriously hard to peg back. The prominent profile benefits most: Bleep Test can slot in just off the leader and mount a straightforward challenge, while Creative Queen, who has form over this C&D configuration, can travel in the slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to string the field out and genuine closers find the six furlongs sufficient to unleash a run.
scenarios.body: Mae Amor is the most interesting profile here — she has a win at 6f Good in her hist and races with visor, suggesting she can produce a concentrated late effort if she gets daylight; Rogue Attraction also carries a win at 6f Good and has been placed at a high level, giving her the class to pick up late if the tempo is honest. The scenario requires a stronger early gallop than Cotai Belle alone is likely to generate, making this the conditional shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Belle fails to sustain her early effort and fades, allowing a prominent-to-midfield type to swoop.
scenarios.body: Creative Queen has the trainer form (Haggas T14:10/56), a win at 6f on recent going, and races with a hood — suggesting she is tuned for a sharp effort mid-race that can capitalise on a faltering leader. Bleep Test's consistent placed record at 6f Good also keeps her relevant if the race fragments into a scramble in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses (Ormolulu, D Flawless, Dandy Magic) successfully settle deep and produce a strong final-furlong finish despite the compressed pace.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability shape precisely because all three are racing out of their natural role — their STYLE_FIT flags (0.91–0.93) confirm they are unlikely to find the ideal position in this race structure. D Flawless has genuine 6f form (a win at 6f Goodish in hist) and headgear (hood) to aid focus, making her marginally the most credible of the three, but the race shape actively works against all of them.

watchPoints.text: Cotai Belle (Ethan Tindall): if she is allowed to coast along unchallenged in front, watch whether she is asked to quicken early or conserved — a slow-burn lead on Good ground over 6f can make her very hard to catch.

Dandy Magic (Jake Dickson 7lb claim): ran just three days ago and is a hold-up horse now mapped into midfield — watch the paddock for any sign of staleness; a sluggish start could leave her detached at the wrong end of a compressed field.

Ormolulu and D Flawless: both are genuine closers who cannot get their preferred position in this race — watch in the early stages whether either horse is restrained and loses ground unnecessarily, as that would effectively rule them out over just six furlongs.

Creative Queen (Paul Mulrennan): races with a hood for William Haggas who is firing at 10/56 over the last 14 days — watch whether she is deployed with mid-race aggression rather than a pure waiting ride, as her style tag (U) suggests she may be ridden to suit the shape rather than habit.

Bleep Test (Sean Kirrane): Tim Easterby's yard form is outstanding (T14:15/104) and the filly has placed at 6f Good four times recently — watch whether she can attach herself to Cotai Belle's quarters from the outset, as that stalking position is the race's second most advantageous slot.

races.name: Dalston 'Confined' Handicap

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Consistent top-ten finisher on Good ground over 7f for Jim Goldie but has not won or placed in five similar-going starts; aged eight and well beaten last two, his true hold-up style is further disadvantaged here with the pack pushed forward — needs a stronger gallop than Homestrait is likely to provide.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for John Ryan with a placing at 7f on Good and 6f course form; races from the rear and while the going suits, the compressed pace shape weakens the case for hold-up horses unless a strong finisher emerges from the bunched pack.

runners_data.name: Record Day
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison three-year-old wearing headgear, placed once from six similar-going starts; best effort was a third over 5f on Standard and the step to 7f on turf with a hold-up style in a moderate-pace race is not ideal, though Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim offers some compensation.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby four-year-old fresh from five days ago, placed on Good ground and capable over 6f; racing in headgear and genuinely a hold-up horse in style, but the tight tempo means this runner is being asked to operate far closer to the pace than it naturally would, which blunts its chief weapon.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Jason Hart's five-year-old has placed three times over 7f on similar going and twice hit the frame specifically at this trip on Good; a genuine hold-up type who actually gets to race close to its natural position here, and the combination of proven 7f form and course-going suitability makes this one of the stronger profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Judicature
runners_data.note: Joel Parkinson & Sue Smith four-year-old placed at 2/10 on soft and 4/10 on Good — solid ground credentials but very much a finisher by nature; the redistribution into midfield means it cannot fully express its closing style, and its chance depends on whether any genuine pace develops in the final stages.

runners_data.name: Albeseeingyer
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's seven-year-old boasts the best similar-going record in the field — 11 from 15 starts on Good, including a win and four placings over 7f; though by inclination a hold-up horse operating further forward than it would like, its sheer familiarity with these conditions makes it credible if it secures a clean run from a handy position.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner for Brian Ellison, uncontested and free to dictate on Good ground over 7f where it has placed in four of five starts — the shape of this race is built around it; Cam Hardie can govern every aspect of the contest, and the horse's recent near-miss form (2-2-2 across last three 7f starts) underlines genuine competitiveness from the front.

runners_data.name: Dakota Breeze
runners_data.note: Archie Watson three-year-old with only four runs to its name, placed once over 7f on Standard; a genuine hold-up horse by style but with very limited form at this trip on turf Good, and racing out of its natural position in the pack makes evaluating its chance difficult — open to improvement but raw.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: David O'Meara three-year-old who has run six and four times over 7f on Good without a placing; freshened after six days and the seven-furlong Good profile fits the race, but consistent mid-division finishes and no wins or placings on comparable going suggest it needs others to underperform.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey three-year-old with a second over 7f on Good in its history and capable of running into a place; operating further forward than its natural style and reliant on positional fortune, though Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps offset the weight burden and a wider draw could assist if it avoids the midfield scrimmage.

runners_data.name: Top Lad
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby three-year-old returning after 85 days off — the longest absence in the field — with only one run on Good going from six starts; a hold-up horse mapped into midfield with minimal turf Good form and a significant fitness question, making this a very speculative profile at this stage of its career.

races.paceDynamic: Homestrait is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Cam Hardie should be able to dictate from the gates at a measured, controlled tempo over Carlisle's flat seven furlongs. That sustainable gallop means the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, reducing the premium on stamina and increasing the chance that a well-placed prominent or mid-division horse can travel into the race without burning fuel. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Dakota Breeze, Judicature, Albeseeingyer, Fan Mail, Supreme Clarets and Top Lad are all natural hold-up horses who cannot all operate from their preferred rear position and will be forced to race closer than ideal, creating congestion in the midfield pack. This race shape heavily favours a horse that can track the lone leader in a handy position without exerting early energy, making the prominent-to-mid-division profile the sweet spot, with Homestrait itself — already on a retrieval mission from an uncontested lead — the standout tactical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Homestrait Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Homestrait is allowed to stride clear from the start and sets an unhurried, controlled tempo that keeps the chasing pack stretched without ever sprinting.
scenarios.body: Hardie dictates every yard on a horse who has placed in four of his last five on Good ground at this trip, and with no rival willing or able to press him, the race becomes a test of who can pick him off closest to home; horses racing prominently just off the pace are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield pack produces an unexpected strong finisher who threads through in the final furlong as Homestrait's solo lead flattens.
scenarios.body: A genuinely moderate pace set by Homestrait means the hold-up horses lose their primary weapon — a strong, honest gallop — but if enough of the redistributed types fail to accelerate early enough, the field concertinas and a horse with a sharp turn of foot can emerge late; Albeseeingyer's four placings from eleven starts on Good ground and Ecclefechan's course-distance form make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Homestrait's rider, feeling pressured by the advancing midfield, lifts the tempo mid-race and turns it into a genuine test of seven furlongs on Good ground.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop filters out the less-exposed and less-stout finishers, rewarding horses with proven 7f stamina and sound recent form at the trip; Black Storm's three placings over 7f on similar ground and Homestrait's own strong track record at the distance make both relevant.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched midfield becomes a traffic problem in the straight and a horse with a wide draw or clean run simply outruns the congestion.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, the straight can become chaotic, and a horse that secures an outer position early — such as Supreme Clarets or Dakota Breeze — avoids the worst of the scrimmage; neither has dominant form but both have the profile to benefit from positional good fortune.

watchPoints.text: Homestrait (Cam Hardie) is the single pace-setter in an 11-runner chasing pack — if Hardie senses no pressure and dials the tempo down through the opening three furlongs, the race could become dangerously slow for closers and almost impossible to peg back in the straight.

Albeseeingyer (Oisin Orr) has the strongest record on similar going in the field (11/15 on Good, 7f specialist) but is being asked to race off its ideal hold-up position — watch whether Orr slots onto the outside of the midfield pack rather than burying it deep, as that decision will define its winning chance.

The bunched midfield of redistributed hold-up types — Dakota Breeze, Judicature, Fan Mail, Supreme Clarets, Top Lad — creates a real traffic-management risk in Carlisle's short straight; any horse drawn wide or that travels on the outer avoids the worst of the scrimmage and gains a meaningful positional advantage.

Black Storm (Jason Hart) is one of the few runners whose hold-up style is not redistributed and whose course-going form (three placings over 7f on Good) genuinely fits the race shape — watch for Hart to track Homestrait at the head of the chasing group rather than getting trapped in the midfield mass.

Top Lad's 85-day absence is the standout fitness flag in the field; if it shows signs of ring-rustiness early and checks up behind the midfield bunching, it could cause interference for the horses immediately behind it in the straight.
